lines.line: -All set. Zhenya, get off that stack. Did you hurt yourself?
-No, I'm fine.
After making a circle around the square, the investigator approached me.
Are you saying you didn't push her? She was just living her life, enjoying it, and suddenly - stepped into the fire?
-That's how it was... Why would I lie?
-And what about girl jealousy? Jealousy is a powerful feeling. You know how many cases like this I've had to investigate...
-That's nonsense! Nothing could be worse for me than what happened to Sonya... She's my best friend. She was, and she always will be!
-I don't know what's in your head. Right now, the main theory is that you helped her fall into the fire.
-Our job is to confirm or disprove that. That's why we're filming a live-action experiment.
-You're all lying. You've already made up your minds just to check it off... All of this. Ask Sonya, for god's sake...
-Even if she's not lying about losing her memory... You've already got a trail of bodies and accidents behind you. This isn't just random.
-I promised to visit Sonya every day. I don't want to go to jail...
-Alright, alright, calm down.
-Phew, guys, let's take a break. I'm tired of you all.

Since that day, I constantly feel like I'm on a leash. Police officers always following me, cameras watching everywhere... And thoughts of Sonya.

I visit her all the time, can't step away. I keep thinking... This couldn't have happened. This is just a dream, or really some kind of simulation.

And Sonya is really just sitting on some swings waiting for me somewhere.
Zhenya pulled me out of my thoughts. Here she is again.
-Hey, how are you? We've already played a third of it. Not much left...
-Not good. Leave me alone.
-What's wrong?
-Nothing.
-I know you're hurting... Shall we be sad together? Can I give you a hug?
-Do you not understand words?
I gritted my teeth in anger.
-I understand, I know you want to be alone.
-Exactly.
-But friends should help each other, you know. Let's go drink some tea, Sanich made some.
-We're not friends.
-But... We've been together all week...
-Give me that bunny! It's not your toy! And stop, stop talking like her!
-No, it's my bunny!
-You're already annoying me!
Without thinking, I punched Zhenya somewhere in the stomach, making her bend over and whimper.
-You're not Sonya. And you'll never replace her. Even a thousand of you wouldn't.
-Even if you put on her clothes and carried her toy all damn week, it changes nothing.
By pretending to be the victim, Zhenya actually becomes one... God, I hope she stops bothering me.
I'm so sorry the investigator didn't make her really jump into the fire.
I walked over to the cop.
-Can I see Sonya?
-Do you think she'd want to talk to you?
I nodded.
-Alright then... That's it for today.

We climbed into his car. As usual, I slammed the door too hard, and he scolded me for it.

The hospital isn't far. Even though I've visited Sonya several times, I can't get used to it. I mean, can I handle it?

And though it's hard to see her like this... I'm ready to do anything just to see her again, even through a window. Sonya...

Yes, it's incredibly hard for her now, but she's alive, alive! But what if suddenly... She'll just... be gone? Just like that... here one moment, gone the next.

A mute, lifeless body with sharp features. What could I do? I'd die with her.

The cop escorted me to the entrance. Not because he's polite... He doesn't want me to run off.

The horrible, soul-chilling sterile air with the taste of medicines and alcohol. It chokes me and turns me inside out.

I could walk to Sonya's room with my eyes closed. They let me in to see her. In the hallway, there's a sweet soapy smell.

Something sharp hits my nose, nasty and somehow strange, inhuman. I've never been in an apartment with a week-old corpse, but that's all I can think of as I breathe in.

After a moment, feeling a chill in my heart and trembling, I push open the door.
Sonya jerked her whole body, the straps shook, and her heavy, gurgling breathing quickened.
-Mira... You came... again... I'm so... so... glad to see you. It's so... horrible here. I missed you so much!
Last time they gave Sonya so many sedatives and painkillers that she could barely speak or understand me.
-Sonya! How are you? How's everything?
I tried to keep it together, to hide the horror I felt just looking at her. No matter how I tried, the tremor in my voice probably gives me away completely.
She's been here a month. Almost immediately, they amputated Sonya's charred limbs. That was the first time I heard that horrible word "stump."
I heard she only had a few hours left, and the fact that she's still breathing is some kind of miracle. I knew she'd survive. I never thought about saying goodbye to her.
-The doctor said... he... doesn't understand why I'm still alive...
-I... should've... died a long time ago.
-With burns like these... you don't survive... To me... it's a curse.
-I shouldn't...
-Oh, come on... Don't talk like that.
I almost burst into tears right in front of her.
-I'm just glad I can still see you.
-I can barely... sleep, but today... today I finally drifted off just before dawn. You know...
-I saw a dream. It was... like I wasn't asleep, like... I could feel everything just like before. I could feel my hands... and my legs...
-I dreamed of the sky. The sky before dawn. So beautiful. And a field... with tall grass.
-And you and I... swinging on squeaky colorful swings. It was so nice... and funny.
-Then... in one moment, it all went dark, and I... fell into an abyss, into a crack in the concrete. And I woke up.
-We'll swing together again on the swings... Don't worry.
-I wish so much... to see the sunrise with you.
-Oh... You can't imagine... how much it hurts... The pain blends into a noise. I can't... think clearly...
-You don't know how shameful it is... when they wash me in some solution... and I'm completely naked... Or...
-When I call a doctor for hours... And when I can't stand it anymore, I... I have to pee on myself. It's... It's so awful.
-What can I do for you?
-I constantly... think... how terrifying it is to die. How terrifying it is when... when you lose everything you had.
-Losing friends... Losing you. And myself. But... at the same time... it's so hard. I can't take it anymore.
-Mira, please, I beg you. Turn... it this all garbage off... so I can finally die...
-No! No way!
-It feels... like my wounds won't heal... But it's not getting worse... either.
-If I suddenly get better... I'll spend my whole... life... in bed... No... Nothing could be scarier.
-No... I'll come to see you every day. I'll be there with you.
-I'll take you for walks in our yard in a wheelchair... I'll feed you treats if you can't eat them yourself.
Sonya began to snort loudly, fighting back tears that were about to roll down her cheeks.
She burst into tears, started sobbing and screaming something incoherent as loudly as her lungs would allow.
There's nothing I can do... There's such pain and hopelessness in her cries. It... tears my soul apart.

Can this be real... Really...
I can't believe this is all real, that we both have to endure this nightmare.
She thrashed as if wanting the rollers with ropes to come off the ceiling, so she could fall to the floor and maybe, break.
The catheters popped out of her veins, and the IVs fell onto the tile.
Medics ran in, and I had to leave.
Old man probably still outside, waiting for me. I don't want to go with him. I don't care what they think.
My eyes eagerly searched for a way to escape, and finally, I saw opened window. Without waiting for the doctors' reaction, I jumped out and found myself outside.
My legs carried me. I don't know where. I'll trust them, like always.
And yet, no matter how much she wants to end it all... I can't let her. I just can't! How could I...
Kill the person I spent my entire childhood with. The one I have so many good memories with... She is my life!
No. I'm sorry, Sonya. No matter how much you're suffering... I can't. Maybe it's selfish, but so be it. I still can't betray myself.
Could she have jumped into the fire on her own? Sonya? I'd never think she'd do that.
Then... something happened to her... Could it be from that injection? Maybe, but... I didn't have that reaction. So, there's something else...
I didn't notice how I ended up in front of her house.
I want to see how her apartment looks...
Everything here is just as it was before the festival. Impenetrable mess and chaos. No trace of the police search.
I sat down on the bed and sank into the old mattress.
-I'd give anything, everything I have, just for you to be alive.
-Why?!
-Why did you do it?!
-Fuck you! Why do you hate me so much?
I shouted, and my scream vanished into the abyss, instead of turning into an echo, bouncing off the walls.
-Huh?
A huge hole gaped in the floor in front of me.
-Where... did this come from... Did Sonya scratch it out?

You could easily fall in... If I jumped down, I could go through easily.
How... deep is it?
I picked up a piece of concrete and threw it into the mouth of the abyss.
It swallowed it, and a second later, there was a sound of it hitting something solid. Looks like I could jump.
I lowered my legs down. They were enveloped by uncomfortably warm air.
Alright. I'm jumping.
Exhaling, I lowered my legs down... And someone caught me by the hand.
Damn, it must be the old man. I need to close doors behind me...
I turned around and saw a figure in a hood.
-Is it you? Again? I almost forgot you...
He nodded and sat down beside me.
-I've been tracking you this whole time.
-You sound like a stalker.
I looked for a moment to run away.
-The police were following you all the time. Can I stay with you?
-Huh?
Strange request. My palms were sweaty from nerves.
Fine. Let him come with me. Nothing worse can happen, because... It already has.
-Alright. I'm going first.
-You? You're a girl.
-Yeah, so?
He thought about it but couldn't find an answer.
-Yeah, nothing.
-Do you have a flashlight?
-Nope.
Fantastic. Diving into darkness with a stranger. What am I thinking?
-We'll have to feel our way through.
Jumping down, I grabbed the collar of his jacket. My eyes started to adjust, and I saw flickering consoles and lights in a concrete corridor. Doesn't look like an ordinary basement.
My companion didn't say a word. I don't even know his name... I only jumped down here with him because I've never felt this much despair.
-So how is she?
-Sonya?
-Mhm.
-You know everything.
-Come on, chill.
-Where did you even come from?
-Well... The commander sent me home.
-Did you fight in a war?
-Nah. Nowhere near...
We walked along the wall toward the brightest light. This place felt eerily familiar...
Sharp bits of concrete poked at my feet, and my head kept almost colliding with another electric box.
-What do you think this is?
-Looks like some kind of bunker. Why do you think there's a bunker under the house?
-Yeah.
-I don't know either...
The glowing spot we'd been walking toward was a doorway. I felt an eerie sense of deja vu, as if I'd seen all this before.
-What's your name?
-Misha. Misha Stepanov.
-I'll try to remember...
-Why have you been following me?
-Well... I wanted to meet you, but it was awkward. And so... This ended up... Ugly.
-Got it.
-Sorry I scared you. Well then...
I looked behind the door.
It's someone's hideout, for sure. Someone was here recently, but now it's empty.
-I'm too late.
We left the room.
-Let's go to the end. And then try to get out.
That's all we can do. We walked further down the corridor. The painted concrete walls grew uglier with every step.
At first there were scuffs, dents, then a few meters later, I nearly tripped on a piece of concrete dangling from rebar. It's like the tunnel crumbles toward its end.
We reached a collapse. The walls had fallen on each other, forming a "house of cards." I decided to squeeze through a triangular opening.
Beyond that, there were no walls at all—only earth and stones. We found ourselves in a real cave. The walls became wet and slimy...
The air was getting more and more stale, and our breathing grew louder. Somewhere, we heard the sound of tram wheels.
It feels as if the walls are moving. I have this feeling that they're made of living flesh.
I feel the pulse of veins and muscle contractions. It... it's alive... All this time... I...
I found it! I found it!
The terrible pain subsides. God, I feel every part of my brain... My head slowly cools down. Something blinds my eyes... So bright...
I open them a little more.
Warm yellow-orange cheerful light dances on my retina through the tall grass.
It can't be... It can't be!
It's sunrise!
Sunrise!
I wanted to scream at the top of my lungs.
People, look, the sun is up! This endless night is finally over...
I got up on all fours.
Sun, dear, warm, I missed you so much. I missed you...
Sun, you have no idea what happened while you were gone...
-Mira, are you crazy?
-Sonya?
-Oh, you're alive. Phew.
-You're okay!
-Yeah... What could happen to me? It's you who fell.
Sonya was swinging back and forth on a swing, cluelessly blowing bubbles into a box of grape juice.
-What? Me?
-Yeah. Did you lose your memory or something? You were doing a backflip on the swings, and they broke off. So, shall we go to the hospital? Feeling dizzy? Nauseous?
-Sonya, I'm so happy to see you! We... We're watching the sunrise together, like we wanted! I'm so happy! I love you, Sonya!
-Well, well...
I crawled over and buried my face in Sonya's chest, who was now blushing, and started to cry loudly, sobbing here and there.
-I never told you... But... You're my whole life. I'll never leave you. Never. We'll always be together, you and me.
Sonya probably thought I had a nightmare.
She gently stroked my head.
